The '''2008–09 season''' of the [[Belgian First Division]] (also known as ''Jupiler Pro League'' after a sponsor) was the 106th season of top-tier football in Belgium. The regular season began on 16 August 2008 and ended on 16 May 2009. [[Standard Liège]] were the defending champions.

On 19 April 2009, [[RAEC Mons (1910)|Mons]] were relegated after [[F.C. Verbroedering Dender E.H.|Dender]] beat [[K.S.V. Roeselare|Roeselare]] 3–1 and made it mathematically impossible for Mons to climb into 16th position or higher. [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]] were relegated on 3 May 2009 after a 1–1 draw at home to [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]].

The 2008–09 champions were decided in a playoff because Standard and Anderlecht finished the regular season equal on points and number of wins. Standard won the playoff by 2–1 on aggregate and thereby retained the title.

==Participating teams==
The league consisted of 18 teams, the best 16 teams from [[2007–08 Belgian First Division|last season]] and two promoted teams from the [[Belgian Second Division|Second Division]].

The number of participants was reduced to 16 teams the season after, hence relegation was increased from two to three or four teams.

===Team changes from the previous season===
[[K. Sint-Truidense V.V.|Sint-Truidense]] and [[FC Brussels|Brussels]] were relegated to the Second Division at the end of the previous season after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by Second Division champions [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] and [[Belgian Second Division final rounds 2001–10#2008|promotion playoff]] winners [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]].

===Championship playoff===
Since Anderlecht and Standard were tied on both points and wins, a two-legged playoff was played in order to determine the league champions. [[Standard Liège|Standard]] won the playoff 2–1 on [[Aggregate score|aggregate]] and were crowned champions.

===Positions by matchday===
Note: The classification was made after the weekend of each matchday, so postponed matches were only processed at the time they were played to represent the ''real'' evolution in standings. These postponed matches are:
* Matchday 1: Mechelen vs. Club Brugge (played between 4th and 5th matchday)
* Matchday 2: Club Brugge vs. Zulte-Waregem (played between 8th and 9th matchday)
* Matchday 13: Kortrijk vs. Zulte-Waregem (played between 16th and 17th matchday)
* Matchday 19: Gent vs. Anderlecht (played between 22nd and 23rd matchday)

==Season statistics==

===Scoring===
* First goal of the season: {{flagicon|Democratic Republic of the Congo}} [[Dieumerci Mbokani]] for [[Standard Liège]] against [[F.C. Verbroedering Dender E.H.|Dender]] (16 August 2008)
* Widest winning margin: '''6''': [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] 7–1 [[KV Mechelen|Mechelen]] (25 October 2008) and [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]] 0–6 [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]] (21 February 2009)
* Most goals in a match: '''8''': [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] 7–1 [[KV Mechelen|Mechelen]] (25 October 2008)
* Hat-tricks scored:
** {{flagicon|France}} [[Idir Ouali]] for [[R.E. Mouscron|Mouscron]] against [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]] (13 September 2008)
** {{flagicon|Argentina}} [[Nicolás Frutos]] for [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] against [[KV Mechelen|Mechelen]] (25 October 2008)
** {{flagicon|France}} [[Habib Habibou]] for [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]] against [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]] (22 November 2008)
** {{flagicon|France}} [[Jérémy Perbet]] for [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]] against [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] (29 November 2008)
** {{flagicon|Bosnia and Herzegovina}} [[Adnan Ćustović]] for [[R.E. Mouscron|Mouscron]] against [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] (20 December 2008)
** {{flagicon|France}} [[Kamulete Makiese|Chris Makiese]] for [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]] against [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] (18 April 2009)

===Cards===
* First yellow card: {{flagicon|Belgium}} [[Jimmy Hempte]] for [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] against [[K.S.V. Roeselare|Roeselare]] (16 August 2008)
* First red card: {{flagicon|France}} [[Karim Belhocine]] for [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] against [[K.S.V. Roeselare|Roeselare]] (16 August 2008)
